links.note: Six ritus: the traditional Indian division of the recurring yearly season cycle, which is 30627 (seasons as a fixed annual cycle). Not 30628, which is the weather-or-climate question about seasons.

Altitude and falling temperature. The closed set has concepts for latitude (30632-34) and distance from the sea (30635-37) but none for altitude, so 30631 - the factors-by-scale concept that these are members of - is its only genuine home.
Asks WHY coastal temperatures are moderate and the key is 'the sea acts as a temperature moderator' - 30636's mechanism, not 30635 which is the observed narrower range.
Mawsynram's record rainfall is the chapter's extreme case for one country carrying sharply different climates (30629). 30630 is specifically the Himalayan alpine type.

Western Ghats as a barrier shaping rainfall = relief working at regional scale, held by 30631. The set has no separate relief concept. (Stem is truncated: statements 1-3 are not printed, only the Ghats statement survives.)
Turns on the rays passing more obliquely at high latitude, which is 30634's explanation, not the bare warm/cold rule of 30633 nor the measurement idea of 30632.
'Monsoon failure' only means anything against 30638's point that the country's water and farming depend on those months. 30639 is the etymology, 30640 the mechanism.
The Subhashita is a prayer for timely rain bringing prosperity - the monsoon-as-lifeline concept, 30638.
Equator-to-pole cooling explained by the rays becoming less direct: 30634, the explanation, rather than 30633 which only states the pattern.

Windward heavy rain and the eastern rain shadow of the Western Ghats: relief as a regional-scale factor, 30631. Not 30640, which is the land-sea pressure mechanism that drives the winds rather than what the hills do to them.

Why traditional monsoon-prediction knowledge is worth preserving; this chapter has no local-knowledge concept (that is 30613 in Understanding the Weather), and the value rests on 30638's claim that the monsoon governs water and farming.
'Tropics' is the zone name for the warm belt around the Equator, which is 30633's warm/temperate/cold zoning. 30632 is the measurement of latitude itself.
Urban heat island mitigated by green cover: a purely local factor, which is the 'others regional or purely local' half of 30631.
Matches four Indian climatic zones to cities, so it tests 30629 (one country, several climatic types) rather than 30630, which is only the alpine case.
Asks which listed items are primary determinants of climate (number of rivers is not): that is the factor inventory, 30631.
Definition of ritus as the traditional classification of seasons - 30627.
Recall of six ritus - 30627.
Naming a ritu (Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha ...) - the season cycle, 30627.
One-word altitude/temperature item; same reasoning as the MCQ - no altitude concept exists, 30631 is the factor concept.
'Topography' is the vocabulary of the relief factor, which sits inside 30631's regional/local factors.
Urban heat islands named as warmer pockets inside cities: the local-scale factor in 30631.
Mawsynram recall, same concept as its MCQ twin: India's internal climatic range, 30629.
Festivals tied to seasons and harvest belong to the season-cycle concept 30627; 30638 is reserved for items about the monsoon's effect on water and farming specifically.
Fuel formed from ancient plant and animal remains is 30645's definition of fossil fuels; 30644 is the list of human activities, not what the fuels are.
The model answer is the concentration-versus-spreading of rays, i.e. 30634's explanation, not merely the warm/cold rule.
Reason temperature falls with altitude; altitude has no concept of its own, so 30631.
Microclimate is by definition a purely local climatic factor - the local end of 30631's scale sorting.
Asks for the basic mechanism and the answer opens with land heating and cooling faster than the ocean, which is 30640 verbatim. 30641 is only the winter half, mentioned second here.
Traditional monsoon indicators (Konkan fishermen, Golden Shower flowering); no local-knowledge concept exists in this chapter, so it goes to the monsoon-centrality concept 30638 with its twin MCQ.
Monsoon failure and its effect on farming, water and migration - the dependence 30638 states.
Burning fossil fuels, deforestation and industrial processes is 30644's list of post-1800s human drivers; 30643 is the natural change that preceded them.
Ghats forcing winds to rise and the Deccan rain shadow: relief at regional scale, 30631, for the same reason as the assertion-reason item.
How a microclimate/urban heat island forms - the local-scale factor in 30631.
